passage:
An abandoned border station became a museum after two neighboring countries opened easier travel between them.
Inside were old desks, stamps, signs, and waiting-room benches. Visitors could see how people once had to line up, show papers, and answer questions.
A student asked why the museum kept a place connected to separation.
The guide said borders shape lives. When they become easier to cross, people should remember what crossing once meant.
The station no longer stopped travelers. It helped them understand movement, control, and change.
A building that once divided people can later teach them about connection.
